children: Oil prices are broadly unchanged in afternoon trading, with both crude benchmarks on track for significant weekly losses amid hopes for diplomatic progress toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Front-month November Brent crude is down 1.1% to $105.44 a barrel, while WTI futures are down 1.8% to $92.90 a barrel. Still, supply risks remain elevated, with renewed Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia keeping regional security concerns in focus. Kpler's head of crude analysis, Homayoun Falakshahi, said that "every 'productive talks' headline" should be treated as a short-lived market reaction to fade, rather than evidence of sustained de-escalation, until there is a concrete step such as an asset release, easing of the blockade or an actual resumption of transits. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
